recognize_zh: 箭頭上方的圓形細胞胞質充滿粗大、深紫黑色的嗜鹼性顆粒，顆粒覆蓋並遮住核的輪廓，細胞邊緣也有顆粒突出，這就是嗜鹼性球（basophil）；左上角為嗜中性球可作大小對照。
features: Round cell slightly smaller than neighboring neutrophil, filled with coarse dark purple-black basophilic granules
Granules overlie and obscure the nucleus so that nuclear lobation is not discernible
Granules extend to the cell margin giving a slightly scalloped outline
Neutrophil at upper left, a mononuclear cell adjacent, and larger cells with basophilic cytoplasm at lower right
Background normochromic red cells with scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a basophil (arrow) containing abundant coarse, dark purple-black cytoplasmic granules that obscure the nucleus and extend to the cell margin. A segmented neutrophil at the upper left, an adjacent mononuclear cell and larger cells with basophilic cytoplasm at the lower right edge are also present. Red cells are normochromic. Findings are consistent with a basophil; basophilia on the differential, particularly with immature myeloid cells, should raise consideration of a myeloproliferative neoplasm such as CML.

ddx.vs: Mast cells are larger with a round central nucleus visible between uniform granules and abundant cytoplasm, and are rare in blood outside systemic mastocytosis or mast cell leukemia.
Eosinophils have uniform orange-red refractile granules and a clearly visible bilobed nucleus, rather than dark purple granules obscuring the nucleus.
Toxic granules are fine to medium dark granules in a neutrophil with a visible multilobed nucleus and pink cytoplasm, not coarse granules masking the nucleus.
Stain precipitate also deposits on red cells and background and lies in a different focal plane, whereas true basophil granules are confined to the cell.
